$comment: What the room sounds like. Read by the Python runtime and by the web app,
because both of them speak: the browser asks for a reply out loud and the
terminal client synthesises one. They used to hold separate copies of this
list and a test parsed one language's source from the other to check they
still agreed. Agreement is not something to test for when the two can read
the same file.
How the model was chosen. Measured on this account, same voice, same
sentence: eleven_flash_v2_5 0.7s, eleven_multilingual_v2 1.2s, eleven_v3
2.7s. v3 is the most expressive of the three and a chat is not paying two
seconds a line for it. Flash is the one built for live conversation, and it
speaks 32 languages, so these voices read Spanish perfectly well.
How the voices were chosen, in order.
1. How modern the voice is, which the account will tell you if you ask:
`high_quality_base_model_ids` is how many current model families a voice
is actually supported on. Most sit at 7 or 8. Adam, who led this list for
months, sits at ZERO — an original 2023 voice carried for compatibility
and rendered by nothing current, which is exactly why he sounded flat.
Sarah sits at 3. Neither is here; nothing below is under 7.
2. What the voice is FOR. These are people talking in a room, so
conversational and informative read first. The character-animation and
advertisement voices are left out however good they are: a room does not
need a narrator.
3. How unlike its neighbour each one is. Assignment goes by position in the
sorted group, so an adjacent pair is the pair that has to be told apart.
This alternates woman, man, woman, man the whole way down and spreads
american, british and australian across it.
Ten of them because there are ten personas: a room can deal every one of
them a different person and still give each a voice of its own. All premade,
each verified to synthesise on this account. Every voice in the shared
library answers a free account with `paid_plan_required`, so a list drawn
from there would be silence. What a free account cannot have is a native
ACCENT, not a language.
